_note: sidecar.json — the CURATED half of the xuansi ABI reference (B15 W2-T3, spec §4.14). tools/gen-abi-reference/gen.py combines this with the SYMBOL face parsed from src/xuansi_host.h (the module-side mirror of the firmware's tools/wasm/xuansi_host.h — the signature source) and emits the checked-in abi-reference.json + abi-reference.md. CI regenerates both and hard-diffs (drift-lock): regenerating must be byte-stable, so this file carries NO timestamps. Curated content lives here; signatures live in the header — never duplicate a signature in both.

abi.note: ABI 1 is the 2026-11-11 recarve (B15 ruling): one contract axis — module ABI and bench api_version are the SAME 1. The old abi=1/abi=2 numbers are retired with fw 0.5.0 (wave-3); the recarved table is the unified host table (the i2c x4 + cam x5 families included, the retired camera_* names gone) plus the initial==max memory freeze. During wave-2 both {1,2} still load.
abi.fw_reference: the 0.4.x wave-2 firmware (protocol_ver 7 era) — the host table this reference was curated against
abi.fw_header_source: the firmware's tools/wasm/xuansi_host.h (signature source; mirrored module-side at src/xuansi_host.h in this repo — the mirror is what CI reads)
abi.load_gate_wave2: {1,2} (fw < 0.5.0) — the wave-3 gate is {1} with the recarved semantics
abi.memory_freeze: a module's linear memory must declare max == initial (the static-footprint freeze; the fw loader refuses initial != max and max-absent shapes with the bytes in the refusal)

retired_symbols.camera_frame_get: renamed onto cam_frame_get at the camera migration (geometry now rides the frame call)
retired_symbols._note: kept compilable in the header for historical modules only; a binary importing them is refused at link time (honest refusal, never a silent fallback)

call_convention.module_shape: wasm32 (wasi-sdk, no WASI imports); exports xuansi_abi() -> u32 (the loader calls it at instantiate and refuses anything the gate does not accept), xuansi_alloc(u32 n) -> u32 (linear-memory offset for the host-written args; 0 = refusal), and entry functions fn(ptr: u32, len: u32) -> u64
call_convention.args: the host serializes the caller's arguments as ONE msgpack array, calls xuansi_alloc, writes it, then calls fn(ptr, len)
call_convention.result: the entry returns a single packed u64 = (result_ptr << 32) | result_len pointing at the module's own msgpack result (C has no multi-value returns — the pair rides one i64); len=0 -> Lua nil
call_convention.out_params: every host function returns void — results are written through out-parameters into the module's linear memory (the host bounds-checks and writes directly; the module reads back as ordinary wasm memory). Buffer parameters are linear-memory offsets (u32). Module authors: land out-params in .bss/heap, not wasm stack slots (portable across the interp and AOT lanes)
call_convention.errors: the host error channel is the wasm exception (message prefix xuansi.<fn>) — surfaced at the Lua face as class=rt
call_convention.alloc_convention: the host calls xuansi_alloc on EVERY call-with-args; a bump-only allocator is a hidden per-call budget (~230 calls at small-args scale). Convention: allocations <= 128B reuse one fixed slot (safe — the fw host serializes all wasm calls); larger ones use the bump arena (see any module's ARGS_SLOT_SZ)
call_convention.limits: args/result msgpack <= 8192B each; container depth <= 8; module file <= 256KB; linear memory 256KB initial default (per-module pinnable), max == initial (the freeze)

value_domain.note: the msgpack<->Lua value bridge, post-float revision (B15 W2-T1): binary64 is the single float caliber
value_domain.kinds: nil, boolean, integer (int64), string, array, map, float64
value_domain.float64: msgpack f64 (0xcb) both ways — eval/submit/job values and wasm call args/results. float32 (0xca) stays OUT of domain (landing it would silently lose precision)
value_domain.non_finite: NaN and +/-Inf are honestly refused at the bridge — 'float value must be finite (JSON/msgpack carry no NaN/±Inf); rescale or send as {sign,exponent,mantissa} integers'
value_domain.mixed_keys: mixed/non-string map keys are out of domain (rt); depth > 8 is out of domain (rt)

lifecycle._note: two axes: the instance table and the hardware claims — they are NOT the same thing
lifecycle.load: instantiates (after the abi gate + the initial==max memory gate + the admission pre-check: sum(loaded footprints) + candidate vs wasm_memory_budget_bytes — the refusal carries the full arithmetic); claims nothing (first host call claims)
lifecycle.unload: destroys the instance, releases NOTHING else — pin/bus claims survive (owner=wasm, loader session); a DVP camera stream also survives (board-level resource, not instance state)
lifecycle.session_reset: unloads every instance of the loader session AND releases its claims (incl. i2c pins and the DVP stream via the teardown chain)
lifecycle.vm_reopen: instances SURVIVE (board-level resource); claims released to a safe state and re-claimed on next host call; SPI slot configs are lost — the module must re-run spi_config
lifecycle.script_death: instances survive (their claims' owner is 'wasm', not the script name)
lifecycle.claims_discipline: gpio/spi/i2c claims live for the module's whole loaded lifetime; cam pins (xclk + 11 DVP) are claimed owner=camera at cam_start/cam_xclk and released by cam_stop (idempotent) or the teardown chains

error_faces.classes: api / rt / oom / compile / budget / timeout / protocol
error_faces.api: name-domain/file/magic/export/abi/mismatch/duplicate/instance-table/file-size/not-loaded/no-such-fn refusals at the loader face; messages carry the [api] prefix
error_faces.rt: marshalling domain (over cap, depth > 8, out-of-domain values), xuansi_alloc refusal, out-of-bounds result pointer, wasm traps (message passed through), and EVERY native host refusal (prefix xuansi.<fn>)
error_faces.oom: Lua VM heap cap exceeded (class=oom, refusal carries the effective cap; see lua_heap_max)
error_faces.budget: eval/script budget exceeded — the refusal reports the numbers ('cpu budget exceeded (budget %u ms; per-call budget_ms 1..30000 or budget.set)')
error_faces.admission: the load() pre-check refusal carries the arithmetic: loaded + candidate vs budget, with the unload-or-shrink fix in the message
error_faces.never_silent: no silent fallbacks anywhere in this contract: a refused .aot never degrades to .wasm, a refused ABI never loads an older lane, OOM never truncates silently

lua_boundaries.rule: budget is a wall clock, reset per tick, and blocking counts
lua_boundaries.detail: the eval/script budget measures WALL time including time blocked inside a native call — a blocking call inside a tick eats the budget just like a spin loop. Per-call override: budget_ms 1..30000 on eval/submit; session budgets via budget.set (0..4000). The refusal reports the numbers.

values crossing the bridge (eval/submit/job value, wasm call args/results) are nil/bool/int64/string/array/map/float64; integers exact to |v|<=2^53; NaN/±Inf refused with the rescale hint; float32 never lands.

coroutine.yield cannot cross a require boundary (require is a C boundary). Resident-script pattern: /drv/*.lua modules do setup + timer registration and RETURN; the yield loop belongs to the launcher script.

every wasm call-with-args consumes xuansi_alloc; the bump arena never gives memory back. Polling modules reuse a small-args slot (<= 128B) or exhaust the heap in ~230 calls. This is a module-author contract, invisible at the Lua face until it bites.

lua_boundaries.rule: 16 timers, globally shared; queue overflow drops are console-only
lua_boundaries.detail: the 16 timer slots are shared across ALL scripts; the per-owner event queue holds 16 entries and overflow DROPS (logged to console only — the Lua face never sees the loss). Design polling cadence against shared scarcity.

lua_boundaries.rule: script lifecycle reaches the events face
lua_boundaries.detail: script started/finished/killed events (source=script) reach the events face; killed carries the cause (budget/error/stop). A budget-killed script's verdict rides the event, not the eval reply.

lua_boundaries.rule: synchronous ops stand silent; slices keep the box alive
lua_boundaries.detail: a synchronous op is silent on its connection for its whole run; internal waits are sliced <= 100ms with watchdog feeding. Hard walls: the conn-task watchdog (5s) and budget.set (0..4000). Long work belongs on submit (async, job events carry the result).

bench.wasm.unload destroys the instance but no pin/bus claims (owner=wasm, loader session) and no DVP stream. Claims release on session_reset (which ALSO unloads the session's instances — the cleanup ritual is unload -> release pins -> session_reset).

bench_signatures._note: the Lua bench face an agent drives; the per-family op lists mirror the fw registration table (single source: the X-macro that also fills caps primitives.<prim>.ops). R4 of the host-side lua lint checks bench.* members against this table.

wasm.semantics: instantiate /drv/<name>.aot|.wasm (the .aot preferred when both exist); gates: abi, initial==max memory, admission arithmetic
the marshalling convention above (msgpack array in, packed u64 out)

wasm.sig: bench.wasm.info(name) -> {abi, loaded_by, session, mem_bytes[, aot='psram', text_bytes, pool_bytes]}
wasm.semantics: identity + the static footprint trio (.aot lane carries text/pool)

wasm.sig: bench.wasm.xfer(src_name, src_off, dst_name, dst_off, len) -> n
wasm.semantics: cross-instance memcpy with explicit ownership (no sharing, no escape); len=0 is a legal no-op; src==dst self-move uses memmove semantics; bounds checked against each instance's CURRENT extent

wasm.sig: bench.wasm.plan(names) -> {rows=[{name, mem_bytes, text_bytes?, pool_bytes?}], loaded_bytes, total_bytes, budget_bytes, fits}
wasm.semantics: admission dry-run — zero side effects; compare against budget before loading. total_bytes is the union of loaded and candidate footprints — an already-loaded candidate is counted once, so planning a loaded module projects zero growth

clock.semantics: boot milliseconds (wraps at 49.7 days) — the Lua-face timing source (a hclock wasm module is no longer needed for this)

meta.semantics: the caps table: fw/api_version/batch, primitives.<prim>.ops, pins.banned, limits (the numeric full table — see caps_keys), heap
the bench API version constant (= 1, the same single axis as the module ABI post-recarve)

families._note: op lists per family (the caps primitives face); full per-op semantics are each primitive's frozen page

caps_keys.note: per-call budget_ms cap (the budget_ms request key 1..30000)
the Lua VM allocator cap in KB (diag.cap adjustable; 0 = unlimited; boot default 4096)
the SURGERY .aot text PSRAM exec window (drops while a surgery container is loaded, recovers on unload)
timer slots shared across ALL scripts (Lua boundary #5)
per-owner event queue depth — overflow DROPS, console-only (Lua boundary #5)
the Lua heap cap in bytes (boot default 4194304; diag.cap 0..65536KB, 0 = unlimited) — the account the OOM refusal reports
current Lua VM heap live bytes
the WAMR pool total account — the admission budget sum(footprints) is checked against (the account is live: load/unload maintain it; the pool itself is fixed at boot)
instance-table mapper slots (the memory account is the governing limit; a full table is the mapper's last-line api refusal)
NOTE key (not a limit): the ADC2 x WiFi gate status string, one of two frozen strings

caps_keys_note: 18 keys in caps.limits (17 numeric + adc2_note), identical across the three exits (Lua bench.caps / msgpack caps op / console CAP: lines). Same keys, same values, same order — any drift is a bug.
